description: Company Description We’re Checkout.com. You might not know our name, but companies like eBay, Spotify, Klarna, Uber, and Sony do, because we’re behind many of the digital experiences you use every day. We are where the world checks out, enabling over 10 billion transactions yearly for more than one billion global shoppers. Whether you want to book a holiday, order food, renew a subscription, or check out online, there’s a good chance our tech powers the payments behind the scenes. Our platform helps the most ambitious businesses deliver effortless digital experiences, at scale. If you want to do career-defining work, you’ve come to the right place. We move fast, think globally, and believe great teams are built by hiring exceptional people with conviction, curiosity, and the desire to make an impact. With 20 offices across six continents and London as our HQ, we’re shaping the future of fintech – and we’re just getting started. The role We are seeking an exceptionally organized, tech-forward Talent Operations Associate to join our Global Talent Acquisition team. As our Talent Operations Associate in London, you will bridge the gap between ensuring our recruiters, and interviewer community are able to find the best talent, through cutting-edge Talent Operations. We are seeking a proactive AI and automation expert to transform our hiring operations. In this role, you will leverage emerging tools to streamline scheduling, resolve logistics challenges, and build data-driven dashboards. If you thrive on solving complex problems, engaging consultatively with senior stakeholders, and redefining talent operations, we want to hear from you. Key Responsibilities Data reporting: handle regional and departmental data reporting, and produce reports and dashboards for the talent acquisition team AI, automation & workflow optimisation: use AI tools and automation to remove manual bottlenecks, hunt for friction points in daily operations, and redesign workflows toward an admin-zero environment. TA Ops projects:Work on a range of strategic projects as needed for example interviewer training, implementing new tooling or designing refined TA processes. Additional Responsibilities Data quality: perform regular data-quality checks to keep reporting accurate and reliable. Ashby / ATS ownership: own and configure Ashby within agreed standards and controls, testing new features and AI integrations to improve pipeline velocity. Contract configuration: configure the contracts for your region and update them as Legal and the People team make changes in Ashby, and build addendums (e.g. start date) that can live in Ashby. Support the recruiters in your region with Ashby and workflow optimisation: optimise interview plans, set up automations, make sure comms are correct, and unblock recruiter issues as they arise. Process documentation: write SOPs and policies for TA and keep the knowledge base up to date as things move forward. Required Qualifications You’re a curious, analytical and motivated individual either due to graduate in summer 2027 or having graduated within the last 24 months, who is excited to dive into the world of Talent Operations. A Bachelor’s or Master’s degree a related field, or relevant work experience in these fields. Curious Problem-Solving: You enjoy learning about issues, asking questions and doing research to find solutions to complex problems. AI & Automation Proficiency: A demonstrated passion for using AI tools, prompt engineering, or workflow automations Data Fluency: Demonstrated ability to work with data and build reporting dashboards to guide decisions. Executive Presence: Confident, tactful communication skills with the ability to manage senior stakeholders and hold them accountable to timeline commitments. Project Management: Ability to prioritize, organize and manage multiple projects in various stages with ease. Additional Information Bring all of you to work We create the conditions for high performers to thrive, through real ownership, fewer blockers, and work that makes a difference from day one. Here, you’ll move fast, take on meaningful challenges, and be recognized for the impact you deliver. It’s a place where ambition gets met with opportunity, and where your growth is in your hands. We work as one team, and we back each other to succeed. So whatever your background or identity, if you’re ready to grow and make a difference, you’ll be right at home here. It’s important we set you up for success and make our process as accessible as possible. At Proton, we believe that privacy is a fundamental human right and the cornerstone of democracy. Our journey began with Proton Mail, the largest secure email service globally, and has since expanded to include Proton VPN, Proton Calendar, Proton Drive, and Proton Pass. These tools empower individuals and organizations to take control of their personal data, break away from Big Tech’s invasive practices, and defeat censorship. Our work impacts hundreds of millions of lives, from activists on the front lines defending freedom to leaders in governments protecting sensitive information. In some cases, Proton’s services have even been instrumental in saving lives by enabling secure and private communications in high-risk situations.

We value intelligence, learning potential, and ambition in our hiring process. Adaptability is key as we navigate uncharted territories and redefine how business is conducted online. Our AI-driven ecosystem spans 100+ companies across ecommerce, food delivery, fintech and experiences, serving billions of consumers worldwide. Join us in shaping the future of technology at global scale. We want to get much better at using AI tools and data to track what is said about us, manage our relationships, and measure the value of our work. You will join the team as a hands-on AI intern. You will set up tools, build simple workflows and give the team the insight it needs to make decisions faster. It is a practical role with real ownership and direct exposure to senior leaders. Help the Group Communications team use AI and data to work smarter: set up media monitoring, build a shared stakeholder CRM and track the metrics that show our impact. Priority use cases 1. Media monitoring platform Help assess, set up and configure a media monitoring platform, using AI for tagging, sentiment and summaries. Define the search terms, sources and alerts for the Group, key executives and priority topics. Produce regular media summaries and flag emerging issues or opportunities to the team. Test AI tools that make monitoring faster and more accurate, and recommend improvements. 2. Stakeholder CRM: Ventures, Illuminate, AI House India, AI House Amsterdam Design and build a simple, shared CRM for contacts, partners, media and events across the four areas. Train team members to use it and make sure it meets data privacy (GDPR) requirements. 3. Metrics and data tracking Agree a core set of communications KPIs with the team, for example reach, share of voice, sentiment, engagement and event outcomes. Build a dashboard that pulls data from monitoring, social and CRM sources. Produce monthly and quarterly reporting with clear insights for leadership. Automate data collection and reporting where possible to save the team time. What success looks like First 3 months: media monitoring is live with regular summaries, and the CRM structure is agreed and populated. By the end of the internship: the team uses the CRM day to day, a KPI dashboard is in place, and there is clear handover documentation so the tools keep running. What you bring A current student or recent graduate in communications, data, business, computer science or a related field. description:
Pilotez les missions où se jouent les paris IA des grands groupes, et transformez-les en résultats mesurables
L’IA, et en particulier l’IA agentique, figure parmi les priorités des comités de direction. Chez Artefact, nous sommes des makers. “We Make AI Work” : notre métier n’est pas de commenter l’IA, c’est de la faire fonctionner, à grande échelle, au cœur des grands groupes.

Et tout commence par vous.

 

Missions

En tant qu’AI Strategist Manager, vous construisez avec les dirigeants de nos clients une stratégie IA crédible, un modèle opératoire adapté et un programme de transformation qui génère une valeur mesurable. Vous êtes le moteur de nos missions AI Strategy : vous les pilotez en autonomie, en garantissez la qualité, les délais et la rentabilité, faites grandir les consultants qui y sont staffés et développez vos comptes aux côtés des Directeurs et Partners.

Vous commencez là où débute toute transformation IA : par l’ambition du client, son secteur d’activité et ses processus métier, et non par la technologie. Et vous restez un maker : vous ne vous arrêtez pas au slide. Vous construisez vous-même analyses, business cases et démos fonctionnelles (vibe coding, low-code, no-code) que le client peut toucher, et vous développez un domaine d’expertise solide dans un secteur ou une fonction métier.

Vous travaillez main dans la main avec nos équipes Engineering (qui construisent et livrent des solutions d’IA agentique) et nos équipes AI Adoption (qui favorisent leur adoption) : vous définissez les processus cibles et la roadmap, Engineering les construit et les livre, et AI Adoption accompagne les personnes dans le changement, dès le premier jour.

 

Activités & Responsabilités

I. Conception de la stratégie et de la transformation IA

Vous définissez la vision IA et la roadmap priorisée des cas d’usage, challengez la pertinence de l’IA et assumez les arbitrages. Lorsque c’est pertinent, vous conduisez des refontes de processus de bout en bout, en pensant lean avant de déployer l’IA et en mobilisant les équipes Engineering et AI Adoption pour les livrer. Vous concevez le modèle opératoire cible et sécurisez ses conditions de succès.

II. Analyses, business cases & prototypage

Vous concevez et pilotez les travaux d’analyse de la mission, business cases inclus, afin de sécuriser des décisions fondées sur les données et sur les faits, et vous revoyez le travail de l’équipe. Vous prototypez rapidement des cas d’usage pour illustrer la valeur par la démo et aider les clients à se projeter dans la solution finale.

III. Delivery, livrables & collaboration

Vous dirigez les missions au quotidien en donnant de la visibilité aux sponsors clients : vous découpez chaque mission en streams, anticipez les risques et challengez le client lorsque c’est pertinent. Vous produisez en autonomie des livrables de niveau C-suite et des synthèses exécutives, structurez la storyline et veillez au respect des standards de qualité Artefact. Vous orchestrez les équipes Engineering pour la faisabilité technique et les équipes AI Adoption pour ancrer l’adoption sur le terrain.

IV. Relation client & développement commercial

Vous êtes l’interlocuteur de confiance des directeurs métiers et des responsables de projets (Comex-1) : vous cartographiez les rapports de force entre les parties prenantes, animez les restitutions pour emporter l’adhésion et maximiser le NPS client, et gérez les tensions et escalades en préservant la confiance. Vous détectez de nouveaux besoins sur le terrain, construisez le plan de développement du compte avec le Directeur ou le Partner et déclenchez de manière proactive des propositions pour développer les comptes existants, en contribuant aux propositions commerciales et aux soutenances.

V. Équipe & connaissances

Vous encadrez et faites grandir les consultants juniors et seniors, êtes counsellor de plusieurs collègues et participez au recrutement des futurs talents. Vous contribuez aussi à la base de connaissances interne par des articles et des retours d’expérience, et animez des formations internes.

 

Profil recherché
Vous vous reconnaissez si… vous aimez piloter des missions exigeantes de bout en bout, faire grandir une équipe et gagner la confiance de dirigeants, et si vous préférez mettre une démo entre leurs mains plutôt que leur décrire une vision.

  • 5 à 8 ans d’expérience au sein d’un cabinet de conseil en stratégie, en management ou en transformation data / IA.
  • Une formation supérieure de niveau licence ou master, issue d’un cursus académique d’excellence.
  • Une expérience de pilotage de missions complexes, de la vision aux résultats, avec des business cases qui résistent à l’examen d’un Comex.
  • Une solide compréhension des enjeux opérationnels de l’IA (IA générative et agentique, gouvernance, cas d’usage métiers), avec la capacité de l’expliquer simplement à des dirigeants.
  • Une expérience de pilotage de projets de refonte de processus métier, avec une maîtrise avérée de certains processus métier.
  • Une expérience du développement commercial (propositions, développement de comptes, relation avec des décideurs de haut niveau).
  • Une expérience d’encadrement d’une équipe de consultants, avec le goût de faire grandir, de déléguer et de tirer l’équipe vers le haut.
  • Un état d’esprit de maker : aisance avec les outils technologiques actuels et capacité à prototyper rapidement des démos fonctionnelles (low-code, no-code, outils agentiques) qui rendent la valeur tangible pour le client.
  • Maîtrise parfaite du français et de l’anglais (oral et écrit).

 

À propos d’Artefact

Artefact est un cabinet de conseil spécialisé en data et en intelligence artificielle, qui accompagne les entreprises pour transformer ces technologies en impact business concret et mesurable. À la croisée du conseil, de la data et de la technologie, nos 2 500 collaborateurs dans 27 pays mettent leurs expertises en commun pour concevoir, développer et déployer des solutions qui répondent aux enjeux de transformation de nos clients.

Notre accompagnement couvre l’intégralité de la chaîne de valeur : AI Strategy (cadrage stratégique, opportunités à fort impact, trajectoires, modèles opératoires), Engineering (industrialisation, architectures agentiques, produits data) et AI Adoption (conduite du changement, montée en compétences, usage quotidien de l’IA).

Pour en savoir plus sur Artefact, nos expertises et notre culture : https://www.artefact.com

 

Pourquoi nous rejoindre ?

  • De la stratégie à la réalisation

Ne pas s’arrêter aux recommandations : participer à la conception et à la concrétisation de solutions IA répondant à de véritables enjeux métiers.

  • Une collaboration entre expertises

Occuper un rôle à la croisée de la stratégie (AI Strategy), de la technologie (Engineering) et de l'humain (AI Adoption).

  • Piloter ce qui compte

Des missions de transformation IA de bout en bout, au cœur des enjeux des grands groupes, avec une vraie autonomie, une équipe à faire grandir et des comptes à développer.

  • Une trajectoire qui accélère

Un parcours clair vers Senior Manager puis Directeur, dans un environnement d’apprentissage continu axé sur la transmission des connaissances et le pragmatisme technologique.

 

Processus de recrutement

  1. Un entretien de fit RH (45') avec HR / Talent Acquisition
  2. Un business case AI-driven (60') avec un AI Strategist Senior Manager ou Directeur
  3. Un business case de prototypage IA hands-on (60') avec un AI Strategist Senior Manager ou Directeur
  4. Un jeu de rôle AI Strategist Manager (45'-60') avec un AI Strategist Directeur ou Partner
  5. Un entretien de fit final (30') avec un AI Strategist Partner ou Managing Partner

 

Rémunération : 66 000€ à 75 000€ brut annuel (fixe) + 10 000€ de variable, selon expérience et séniorité

 

Chez Artefact, nous sommes convaincus que la diversité des parcours, des expériences et des perspectives fait la richesse de nos équipes. Nous nous engageons à offrir un environnement inclusif et des opportunités équitables, où chacune et chacun peut évoluer et exprimer pleinement son potentiel. Nos recrutements reposent sur les compétences, le potentiel et l’adéquation avec le rôle.

description:
WPP is the trusted growth partner for the world’s leading brands. 

We unite cutting-edge media intelligence and data solutions, world-class creativity, next-generation production, transformative enterprise solutions and expert strategic counsel in a single company – powered by exceptional talent and our agentic marketing platform, WPP Open, to help our clients navigate change, capture opportunity and deliver transformational growth. 
 
We work with the world's most valuable brands and have global reach across 100+ markets, with deep local expertise.
 
Our people are the key to our success. We're committed to fostering a culture of creativity, belonging and continuous learning, attracting and developing the brightest talent, and providing exciting career opportunities that help our people grow. 
 
For more information, visit WPP.com.
 

Why we're hiring:

As part of WPPs Elevate28 strategy, we are accelerating a major Finance Technology transformation to simplify, modernise and standardise the platforms, data and processes that underpin Global Finance. This portfolio is critical to statutory reporting, management reporting, forecasting, planning, control, performance management, compliance, and executive decision-making. 

The Global Programme Director - Finance Technology will shape, govern and drive WPP’s global Finance Technology transformation portfolio. This senior enterprise leadership role turns a complex, multi-year agenda into a coherent roadmap that simplifies the finance technology estate, strengthens control and resilience, and enables faster, more trusted business insight. 

The role spans Finance ERP standardisation, consolidation platform replacement, enterprise performance management, revenue forecasting, analytics, finance data foundations and operating model change. It will work across Group Finance, Enterprise Technology, agencies, markets, regions and delivery partners to align priorities, secure decisions, manage trade-offs and ensure investment delivers measurable enterprise value. 

This is a director-level role requiring strategic judgement, executive influence, commercial discipline and the ability to create clarity, momentum and delivery confidence across a high-profile transformation portfolio. 

What you'll be doing:

  • Shape and sequence the global Finance ERP roadmap, moving WPP towards fewer platforms, common templates, harmonised controls and reduced process variation
  • Lead the transition from legacy consolidation tooling to a resilient enterprise performance management capability across consolidation, planning, forecasting, reporting and analytics
  • Strengthen delivery confidence, investment discipline and benefits realisation across a high-value portfolio with significant executive visibility and business risk
  • Define the global Finance Technology portfolio vision, investment narrative and multi-year roadmap across Finance ERP, consolidation, enterprise performance management, forecasting, analytics and finance data
  • Translate finance transformation priorities into a clear, sequenced and deliverable portfolio that balances strategic value, delivery capacity, affordability, risk and business disruption
  • Establish strong portfolio governance, investment controls, stage gates, assurance and executive reporting to support timely, evidence-based decisions
  • Lead and orchestrate a portfolio of finance transformation programmes, ensuring clear sponsorship, ownership, outcomes, funding, delivery accountability and benefits realisation
  • Manage portfolio risks, dependencies, resources, budgets, delivery confidence and executive escalations across Finance, Enterprise Technology, data, architecture, security, controls, suppliers, markets and agencies
  • Build trusted relationships with senior Finance, Enterprise Technology, agency, market and regional leaders to align priorities, resolve trade-offs and maintain enterprise momentum
  • Shape business cases, funding recommendations and portfolio choices using clear analysis of cost, benefit, risk, sequencing, control impact and business value
  • Manage system integrators, software vendors and delivery partners against commitments, outcomes, commercial levers and performance expectations
  • Lead and coach programme directors, delivery leads, PMOs and matrixed teams to raise delivery standards, strengthen transparency and build a culture of accountability. 

What you'll need:

  • Extensive experience leading large-scale finance technology, ERP, enterprise performance management or corporate systems transformation in a global organisation. 
  • Proven track record of leading multi-year transformation portfolios with significant budgets, multiple delivery partners, complex governance and senior executive sponsorship. 
  • Strong understanding of finance operating models and core finance capabilities, including ERP, consolidation, planning, budgeting, forecasting, reporting, analytics, controls and finance data. 
  • Director-level leadership presence, with the credibility to influence C-suite leaders, Finance executives, technology leaders, agencies, markets and external partners. 
  • Strong capability in portfolio governance, investment management, business case development, budget ownership, benefits realisation, assurance, RAID and dependency management. 
  • Commercially confident, with experience managing vendors, system integrators and delivery partners against commitments, outcomes and performance measures. 
  • Exceptional communication skills, with the ability to simplify complex finance, technology and delivery issues into clear executive insight, decisions and recommendations. 
  • Ability to create clarity in ambiguity, resolve competing priorities and lead matrixed teams across geographies, functions and business units. 
  • Strong understanding of change, adoption, business readiness, service transition, process ownership and operating model embedding. 
  • Resilient, commercially minded and outcome-focused, with high integrity, strong judgement and the confidence to challenge constructively when value, control or delivery confidence is at risk. 

Who you are:

You're open: We are inclusive and collaborative; we encourage the free exchange of ideas; we respect and celebrate diverse views. We are open-minded: to new ideas, new partnerships, new ways of working.

You're optimistic: We believe in the power of creativity, technology and talent to create brighter futures or our people, our clients and our communities. We approach all that we do with conviction: to try the new and to seek the unexpected.

You're extraordinary: we are stronger together: through collaboration we achieve the amazing. We are creative leaders and pioneers of our industry; we provide extraordinary every day.

What we'll give you:

Passionate, inspired people – We aim to create a culture in which people can do extraordinary work.

Scale and opportunity – We offer the opportunity to create, influence and complete projects at a scale that is unparalleled in the industry.

Challenging and stimulating work – Unique work and the opportunity to join a group of creative problem solvers. Are you up for the challenge?

 

We believe the best work happens when we're together, fostering creativity, collaboration, and connection. That's why we’ve adopted a hybrid approach, with teams in the office around four days a week. description: Our team shared’s mission is deploy AI agents to transform how patients and doctors connect We believe healthcare shouldn’t be defined by missed calls, endless waiting lines, and overwhelmed staff. Patients and professionals deserve better. Vocca builds AI voice agents that answer every call instantly, schedule and reschedule appointments, and free up staff to focus on what matters most: care. Already trusted by 15 000+ providers, we’re transforming the patient–provider relationship, one call at a time. Want to shape the future of healthcare? Join us ! Discover our company culture and values Here is a product teaser Eliott's interview for Welcome to the jungle Eliott's quick interview for Speedinvest Articles on our A round (techfundingnews, Maddyness, les echos, our blog) Vocca in a few words Vocca is an AI voice agent that answers 100% of the calls of medical centres. The patient calls, the AI books the appointment or answers the question, and the medical secretaries keep their time for the cases where a human is really needed. $20M raised, with the founders of Alan and Datadog as investors Close to 1 million calls a month going through the platform Opening the US market The problem Every medical practice runs on software that holds its calendar and its patients. There are dozens of different ones. Most were built twenty years ago and some have no API at all. To book an appointment during a call, our AI agent has to read and write in that software in real time, while the patient waits on the line. On several of these systems, Vocca is the only integrator in the world. This is the work with the most direct impact on the business. A clinic whose software is connected to our agent does not switch. Retention, pricing power, our lead over competitors: it all depends on these integrations. Every software we cannot connect is a clinic we cannot sign. The next step is writing back. Today the agent reads and books. Tomorrow it updates records in EHR, PMS and RIS systems, which raises the reliability bar a lot. In the US, we are opening the dental software ecosystem, with the compliance work that comes with it (HIPAA, SOC2). There is no product manager on this scope. You would be the one deciding. What you will own The architecture of our booking layer. Today it is code written provider by provider, under pressure, partly in Python. It is becoming one unified layer in TypeScript that handles the rules of each medical centre, where adding a new software takes days, not weeks. Speed and reliability at close to 1M calls a month. A call to a clinic software can take several seconds, and the patient cannot wait. You decide how we detect a booking failure in a clinic within 24 hours and what a healthy integration looks like. The roadmap of your scope. You decide which software we connect first, with the sales, ops and support teams and the clinics themselves, and you prove it worked with a number: bookings that go through, failures caught, clinics signed. The relationship with the software vendors, in France and in the US. The hard integrations are the ones nobody else wants to do. They are what makes Vocca hard to replace. The team. You define how this scope works (reviews, documentation, technical decisions), you take part in hiring the next engineers and you help them ship in their first week. How we build Experimental, not R&D. You test, you prove with data, you ship. Challenging a decision means coming back with a result, not a debate. Ship, then fix the last 1%. We ship the version that works, then fix the last 1% when it shows up. With AI, this trade off is much cheaper than before. The judgment about what not to touch is yours. AI, seriously. Agents in every workflow, Claude Max provided. A migration estimated at 3 months was done in 2 weeks. Close to the field. You talk every day with the ops team that deploys clinics, the support team that hears when something breaks and, when it matters, the clinics and the software vendors themselves. Stack TypeScript everywhere (Node, monorepo), PostgreSQL, REST and SOAP APIs from software vendors. We are migrating our last Python services to TypeScript over the coming months. description:
About CoLab

At CoLab, we help mechanical engineering teams bring life-changing products to market years sooner.

We build AI for engineers designing cars, medical devices, and jet engines. Products this complex aren't sketched and sent to production. Teams spend months on iterations, reviews, and tests, predicting how every part performs before anything is built. CoLab is where those reviews happen, and we capture the rationale behind every change. Other tools show what changed between versions. Only CoLab knows why. That's how our AI helps manufacturers like Bobcat, Triumph Motorcycles, and GE Appliances make better decisions, eliminate rework cycles, and get to market faster.

Proudly based in St. John’s, Newfoundland, CoLab started with one customer in 2018. Since then we’ve raised a $72M Series C, been named the 57th fastest growing company in North America by Deloitte (Fast 500™), signed multi-year AI partnerships with companies like Bombardier, and grown to a team of 250+.

About the Role

This is a high-impact role that helps define how CoLab delivers technical value to its most strategic customers in Aerospace and Defence. CoLab is a category-creating product, which means adoption isn't just a rollout. It's a change in how the organization works.

In this role, you'd act as a trusted advisor, leveraging people, process, and technology to help teams rethink how they manage feedback, data, and decision-making across design and PLM. That means getting deep into customer workflows, testing new ways of working, and building repeatable methods the rest of the team can scale.

You'll work alongside a Customer Success Manager, and use what you learn on the front line to help shape product direction. This role isn't about selling or pitching. It's about deeply understanding engineering problems and solving them alongside the customer.

We are looking for a candidate in Switzerland to work regularly on-site with local CoLab customers.

Our Ideal Candidate

You’re a mechanical engineer by trade and have worked as a designer in an A&D company. You also understand the full product development life cycle: how design, manufacturing, quality, and engineering leadership depend on each other, and where collaboration breaks down. You can coach those teams toward working together better.

You know how to improve that life cycle with technology. Maybe you’ve championed internal tools or created automation or scripts.

You also know a process that makes sense on paper won’t get adopted on its own. You can meet people where they are, including the stakeholders who don’t want to change.

You don’t need to be the loudest voice in the room, but you can run a sprint and lead a cross-functional project. If the average person might find this job too undefined or complex, that probably excites you.

Job Responsibilities

  • Mapping a customer's current-state design review and engineering workflows, and defining the target-state process their teams will actually adopt.
  • Deploying and tuning CoLab's AI capabilities against a customer's own standards, drawing checklists, and design guidelines, and diagnosing what's working and what isn't.
  • Providing mechanical engineering expertise to validate AI-generated results and ensure engineering rigor.
  • Investigating and solving complex engineering data and integration challenges across PLM, ERP, QMS, and traditional design feedback tools.
  • Expanding adoption into new teams, programs, and sites within the account, partnering with the Customer Success Manager on where the next opportunity sits.
  • Collaborating with product teams to identify feature gaps, improve capabilities, and refine AutoReview.

Qualifications

Must-haves:

  • Background in mechanical design engineering, ideally in a medium- to large-sized organization.
  • Strong understanding of PLM & ERP systems and enterprise engineering data architecture.
  • Demonstrated ability to lead technical projects and cross-functional collaborations.
  • Experience working directly with customers or internal stakeholders to solve technical problems.
  • Comfort working in fast-changing, ambiguous environments.
  • Strong written communication and documentation skills.
  • Working knowledge of high-level AI architecture, specifically LLMs.
  • Familiarity with APIs, data integrations, and enterprise architecture concepts.
  • Located in Switzerland 

Nice-to-haves:

  • Experience with internal tool development, scripting, or automation.
  • Exposure to AI/ML tools applied to engineering workflows.
  • Prior work in design consulting or product development at scale.

Travel Expectations

While this is a fully remote role, travel is a consistent part of the job. There are two primary types of travel you can expect:

  • Team Weeks: Once per quarter, the sales team or entire company gets together in person. These typically involve traveling out on a Monday and returning on a Thursday or Friday. Two of these each year are held at our headquarters in St. John's, Newfoundland, Canada and the others take place in more central locations that evolve as the team grows.
  • On-sites: This role will work closely with a local customer with expectations to be on site with that customer, so there will likely be far less travel than our typical MFDE roll. That being said, in the event the local customer were to no longer work with us, the following is our standard MFDE travel expectations: “For most of our large deployment customers, we will visit on-site during kick-off and key expansion opportunities. Most on-sites involve 2-3 days with the customer, with travel on either side. Travel is primarily within North America, and you can expect 4 customer on-sites per quarter.”

Extra Details

  • This is a full-time, permanent position with a competitive compensation package that includes stock options.
  • Unlimited paid vacation and extended health benefits 

Equity Note

Frequently cited statistics show that people who identify with historically marginalized groups are likely to apply to jobs only if they meet 100% of the qualifications. We encourage you to help us break that statistic and apply even if you don't meet every single qualification. Your potential is what matters most to us.

description: About us We see the semiconductor industry as a realm of possibility. We see opportunity. We see the profound impact that our graphene solutions will have in transforming the industry. We invite you to join us in driving change with our fundamentally human-centered approach, uniting bright minds around a shared vision. The vision is: Prove to everybody that you can make a fundamental change. Prove with your knowledge and skills how things can be done differently. Together, we can change the paradigm of how the world connects About our technology The semiconductor industry’s growing demand for more powerful chips with higher bandwidth and lower power finds its solution in our technology. We connect chips to high-throughput, low-delay computing networks. The key lies in harnessing the physical properties of graphene to combine electronic computing with photonic communication, allowing countless chips to interact almost as if they were one. Our graphene photonic innovation increases computing power and efficiency to a new order of magnitude In short, we connect chips to create powerful and energy-efficient networks, overcoming connectivity limitations in the semiconductor industry. We deliver the graphene solution The Role We are seeking a Package Reliability Engineer to join our team. In this role, you will own the reliability of our packaged products, from defining mission profiles and reliability targets to identifying package-level failure mechanisms, developing qualification strategies, and making evidence-based release recommendations. Reporting to the Quality & Reliability Program Lead, you will work closely with the Package Architecture, Device Reliability, Product Engineering, and OSAT/laboratory partners to translate product use cases into mission profiles and FIT/MTBF targets. You will assess reliability risks, define and execute package-level reliability test plans, lead failure analysis activities, and ensure findings are driven to resolution. Your core focus will be to transform product requirements into robust reliability strategies, validate package concepts through targeted stress testing, and provide data-driven recommendations that enable confident product release. To join our team, you should be excited to: Own mission profiles and reliability targets by defining product operating conditions (temperature, voltage, humidity, thermal cycling, and lifetime requirements) and allocating FIT, MTBF, and lifetime targets across package, interconnect, and device-level contributors. Assess package reliability risks by evaluating failure mechanisms across substrates, die attach, interconnects, solder joints, board attach, and optical/fiber interfaces, including delamination, warpage, fatigue, electromigration, and optical or electrical drift. Define and execute package reliability qualification plans covering thermal, mechanical, environmental, and board-level stress testing in accordance with JEDEC, AEC-Q100/Q006, IPC, IEC, and customer-specific requirements. Lead the technical interface with OSATs, substrate suppliers, and labs, defining reliability requirements, reviewing data, and challenging results when the supporting evidence is insufficient or unrepresentative. Drive root-cause investigations and failure analysis, leveraging techniques such as X-ray, C-SAM, cross-sectioning, SEM/EDX, and related methods, and translate findings into CAPA/8D actions, design improvements, and requalification decisions. Develop risk-based qualification strategies for novel packaging technologies, such as UBC and optical interconnects, where industry standards are incomplete or do not yet exist. Provide data-driven release recommendations by assessing whether products are ready for customer sampling, qualification milestones, or production release, while clearly communicating any remaining reliability risks. Your Qualifications Educational background with a Master's degree (or equivalent experience) in Electrical Engineering, Microelectronics, Materials Science, Reliability Engineering, or a related field. Package reliability expertise with 3–5+ years of experience evaluating semiconductor package construction (substrates, die attach, interconnects, and solder joints) and understanding the failure mechanisms associated with these technologies. Understanding of high-speed I/O and RF reliability, including how reliability degradation impacts high-speed serial, RF, and optical interfaces (e.g., signal integrity, insertion loss, jitter, and eye closure over product lifetime). This expertise goes beyond conventional digital logic reliability and is a core requirement for this role. Experience with photonics reliability is highly desirable. Solid foundation in reliability engineering, including FIT and MTBF calculations, mission profile development, acceleration models, and translating product use cases into measurable reliability requirements and targets. Experience with industry qualification standards, including JEDEC, AEC-Q100/Q006, IPC, and IEC, as well as the judgment to apply knowledge-based qualification approaches when existing standards are not sufficient. Failure analysis expertise, with the ability to interpret results from techniques such as X-ray, C-SAM, cross-sectioning, and SEM/EDX, and translate findings into risk-based recommendations. Experience collaborating with OSATs, substrate suppliers, and external laboratories, including defining technical reliability requirements, reviewing qualification data, and driving technical discussions to ensure robust evidence for product qualification. Excellent cross-functional communication skills, with the ability to clearly communicate reliability risks, trade-offs, and evidence gaps to architects, engineers, suppliers, and leadership. description: quinn is becoming the way people employ, across the globe, through one app. quinn is an app-based, managed payroll and employment-administration service. We run it for private households employing a cleaner, nanny, or caretaker, and for businesses that manage employment relationships at scale. The customer stays the legal employer: quinn registers the employment, runs payroll, and handles social insurance, taxes, and filings on their behalf, automated end to end. Where everyone else sells software, quinn sells the outcome. We don't sell payroll software. We run payroll. The purpose behind it is simple: Fair employment. For all. Correct and fair employment, made simple and accessible for any employer and any employee, in any market quinn enters. Where this is going Think about what Revolut did to banking. All of the complexity (the regulation, the clearing, the compliance) handled invisibly in the background, and one simple experience at the front. Nobody using Revolut thinks about what happens behind the screen when they open a new account, swap currencies or send money abroad. It just works, in a couple of taps. Nobody should have to think about it in order to employ someone either. That is what quinn is building, and it is further along than most people assume: a profitable core business, running today in Switzerland, Germany and the UK, expanding into new markets both by launching and by acquiring. By 2030 quinn intends to be the destination brand for fair employment across six countries and more, on one platform, with one experience. One platform means one frontend. One experience means it looks and behaves like quinn whether you are in Zurich or in London, a household or a company. In this strategy that is not a nice-to-have. It is the strategy. Which is why the surface matters more than anything else. Everything quinn does is designed to disappear. The interface is the only part the customer ever sees, and it is the whole proof that the complexity behind it is really handled. Why this role exists Today, quinn runs on several separate web apps: one per product and market, each with its own frontend, grown over the years as the company grew. Our backend engineers built them alongside everything else, plus an internal admin tool that grew the same way. They all work: thousands of employers run payroll through them every month. But nobody was ever tasked with owning the frontend development, so each one got built the way frontend is built by Backend Developers, seen as a hassle rather than the main aspect users interactive with. What comes next is one frontend that replaces all of them, built from scratch: one quinn app for employers, employees and our own support team, in the browser first, then in the App Store and Google Play from the same work. Alongside it, the frontend of Maestro, the internal tool that replaces the old admin for batch processes. The phone app is the surface that matters most, so everything is built for it from the first screen rather than adapted to it afterwards. That is the opening. How we work We are AI-native, and we mean it operationally rather than as a slogan. AI is how the work gets done here. It is why a small team ships like a large one, and it is a large part of how one person will be able to hold the standard we are describing. We expect you to be at the front of that. Not to have heard of the tools, to live in them, and to build your own leverage with them: scaffolding, visual regression checks, design-token pipelines, whatever takes manual work out of the way. And we expect the judgement that has to come with it. AI writes code that looks right and is subtly wrong: structure that doesn't scale, patterns that fall apart three screens later, components that work once and never again. You take the speed and throw away the rest. AI never lowers the bar here. It is the reason the bar can be this high. Tasks What you will own Everything on the screen: The frontend of the quinn app and the web app. App first. One app for everyone who uses quinn: the employer, the employee, and our own support team working inside the customer's account. The frontend of Maestro, our internal batch tool. Desktop and dense: queues, runs, tables, filters, multi-select, keyboard shortcuts. A different discipline from the app, built on the same components. The component library across quinn Home and quinn Business: one frontend, one experience, every market and every device. Whether the app feels native: response, scrolling, gestures, transitions, biometric login, push. Nothing that gives away it isn't native. The quality of what you ship. Nothing leaves your hands half-finished. Where design ends, engineering begins. We have a design team, and they own how quinn looks and behaves: the flows, the visual design, the tokens, the component specs. You don't design. You own everything from there: how it is built, and everything a design file cannot reasonably specify, such as gestures, keyboard, safe areas, what happens between the drawn breakpoints, the loading, offline, pending and failed states, what a three-line German label does to a layout that was designed for English. You are in the room before design starts, saying what already exists in the library and what a new pattern costs. Not at the end, receiving a handover. When you and design disagree, they decide how it looks and behaves and you decide how it is built. Nothing enters the component library without both of you. Requirements Who we are looking for You care about interfaces more than anyone else in the room. You see the two-pixel misalignment without being told, and it bothers you until it is fixed. You build and maintain UI components and design systems, not one-off screens. You can build a mobile app that feels like one. And you can also build a desktop tool full of tables, filters and keyboard shortcuts, because Maestro is one. You understand UX and how people actually behave, not only how a screen looks. And you write code other people can take over: scalable, structured, documented. Not something that only works while you are in the building. You are independent and decisive. Nobody will spec every detail for you and nobody will review your pixels. You are fluent in English, no other language is required. And if you have a portfolio, a live product, or anything you have shipped that you are proud of, show it to us. Not a requirement, but it tells us more than a CV does. Most importantly: you want this one. Not a frontend role at a company where the frontend is a chore. This one, the app nobody has built yet, the standard nobody has set yet, and a company where getting it right actually decides whether the strategy works. The Team We are a small, fast, direct team. We do not have a lot of process or a lot of hierarchy. We do have a clear strategy, an ambitious plan, and five values we actually mean: Be open, Own it, Speak up, Keep it simple, Bias for action. This is one of the most important hires we will make this year. We are not rushing it and we are not filling a seat. We are looking for the person who reads this and thinks: finally. description: About us We see the semiconductor industry as a realm of possibility. We see opportunity. We see the profound impact that our graphene solutions will have in transforming the industry. Reporting to the Quality & Reliability Program Lead, you will work closely with the Package Reliability Engineer, Product Engineering team, and external laboratories and OSAT partners to plan and execute qualification testing. You will develop test hardware in collaboration with external partners, coordinate the design of test PCBs and fixtures, select and configure test equipment, and ensure every qualification campaign produces accurate, well-documented, and reproducible results. Your core focus will be to transform qualification requirements into practical test solutions, execute high-quality validation campaigns, and deliver the reliable data needed to make confident product qualification and release decisions. Coordinate qualification campaigns with OSATs and external laboratories by managing schedules, sample logistics, and test execution, while providing on-site or remote test supervision where needed Collect, analyze, and document qualification results, producing clear pass/fail assessments, comprehensive test reports, and fully traceable records that contribute to the overall product qualification evidence package. Your Qualifications Educational background with a Bachelor's or Master's degree in Electrical Engineering, Electronics, or a related discipline. Hands-on product qualification experience with 2–4+ years of experience in hardware bring-up, bench testing, or product qualification test campaigns. Experience testing RF and high-speed I/O, including high-speed serial, RF, or optical links using equipment such as vector network analyzers (VNAs), high-bandwidth oscilloscopes, BERTs, and other signal integrity measurement tools. This is a core requirement for the role, as experience limited to low-speed digital or logic circuit testing is not sufficient. Experience with photonics testing is a strong advantage. Proficiency with laboratory test equipment, including oscilloscopes, power supplies, thermal chambers, data acquisition (DAQ) systems, and, ideally, RF and high-speed characterization equipment such as VNAs, BERT, and high-bandwidth scopes. Experience developing test hardware, working closely with PCB design and fabrication partners to define specs, review designs, and support the bring-up of test boards or fixtures. Strong test execution and documentation skills, running test campaigns methodically and writing clean, traceable results. That engine funds everything else on this page. Role summary Catalyst Capital is hiring its first Chief Information Security Officer to own security across every brand in the group. You will set the strategy, build the program, and personally run the response when something goes wrong. The job is two halves. Half is the core of a CISO's role: incident response, identity and access, vendor risk, phishing defense, policy and audit readiness, and the judgment calls only a person can own. The other half is making security AI-driven: mapping our full surface and building agentic systems that test, monitor and audit it with near-total coverage, so security keeps pace as more of the company runs on AI. This is a player-coach role: about half hands-on, leading a small team of engineers. You report to Group leadership, brief the leadership team monthly, and are the person they trust to explain risk in plain language and make the call under pressure. What you will own Core security leadership (about half) Security strategy and program. Own the security strategy, roadmap and budget across Decentralized Masters, Legacy, Inflection Club, Sentinelis and future brands. Report posture, top risks and trends to leadership every month, with a risk register leadership can act on. Incident response. Own IR end to end: detection, triage, containment, eradication, recovery and the postmortem. Lead the room during a live incident and coordinate with legal counsel, forensics firms, insurers and regulators. Keep runbooks current and run tabletop exercises. Cloud and identity security. Own identity and access across the group: SSO, MFA, least-privilege roles, admin redundancy and short-lived credentials. Set the AWS security baseline. Third-party and vendor risk. Assess the security of every vendor and data provider we depend on, including their audits and attestations, and set the bar a vendor must clear before connecting to our systems or data. Platform and customer account security. Set the standards for login protection and account-takeover defense on our platforms, and work with the engineering teams that own each platform to build them in. Phishing and impersonation defense. Own email security, staff training and phishing simulations. Run brand protection: find and take down fake domains and accounts impersonating our brands and leaders. Policy, compliance and trust. Write and enforce policies people actually follow. Prepare the company for SOC 2 or ISO 27001 with Legal & Compliance. Own the public security and trust story, including the trust page on our products. Team leadership. Manage and develop our security engineers, decide what we build in-house versus outsource, and grow the team only where automation cannot do the job. Member scam awareness. Supply the security content behind scam-awareness messaging to members, working with Community, Support and Marketing. Legal approves the wording. AI-driven security (about half) Full attack-surface map. Build and maintain a living inventory of everything we run: internal apps, cloud, code repos, and every SaaS tool and integration (CRM, telephony, community, payments, data providers). Know what connects to what, who has access, and what is logged. Agentic security harness. Design and run AI-driven systems that approach 100% coverage: automated code and dependency review, continuous configuration and access audits, and vendor documentation review. Humans set direction and make the judgment calls; agents do the exhaustive work. AI-driven detection and logging. Own the security stack (SIEM, Rapid7; endpoint protection; email security; identity and device management), make sure every critical system sends usable logs, and use AI to triage alerts and hunt across them. Secure AI and vibe-coding standards. Set the rules for how teams build with AI: what can ship, what data AI tools may touch, and the review path before anything with customer data goes live. AI agent security. As more of the company runs on agents and automations, secure them: scoped credentials and tool permissions, prompt-injection defense, data exposure, and monitoring and guardrails for agents in production. Review high-risk agents before launch, including our own security agents. Scope This role protects our company, our platforms, our data and our brands. For members' personal wallets and accounts outside our platforms, our role is education: helping members recognize and avoid scams. Requirements What you will bring Must have 10+ years in security, including 3+ years leading a security function as CISO, Head of Security or equivalent at a company of 100+ people. Has led live-incident response, not just tabletop exercises, including briefing executives during the incident. Has built or rebuilt a security program from an early stage: strategy, policy, tooling, training and incident response. AI-native operator. Here, your impact doesn’t just power a product; it shapes future generations! What you’ll work on: We’re moving everything towards GCP and Kubernetes. We’re growing towards a scale that no longer matches our legacy architecture and actively investing in modernization. We’re migrating on-premise workloads to GKE, strengthening security and business continuity best practices, and moving toward platform self-service for our development teams. A core goal is to consolidate and shrink the stack, and every migration decision is measured against whether it lowers the daily burden on the team. You’ll need to work with your team balancing both platform initiatives and the operational needs of the engineering teams you serve. You’ll report to our head of engineering and be expected to split your time roughly 50/50 between people management and hands-on development. Prioritization always goes to leading and supporting your engineers. Your team will consist of four engineers. What’s unique about management at Miaplaza: Miaplaza is a US-based education company, which means we probably are doing things differently than you’ve done in your past experience. Here are a few differences you may notice: You will first onboard within your team as a senior engineer for 2 months. You will start to onboard as a manager during month two and will take over the team roughly at 10 weeks. This is non-negotiable as both periods of time are equally important. We expect our EMs to spend approximately 50% of their time hands-on, even after they’ve completed onboarding as a senior engineer. We emphasize the importance of pedagogical principles. A responsibility is to grow your engineers and those around you. One of such pedagogical principles is that we expect you to have full oversight into your direct reports' work; you can’t properly teach if you don’t see the process behind the output. Feedback is the norm. You’ll be expected to give meaningful, specific reinforcement and constructive feedback whenever you notice something. You should also expect to receive feedback. Work with the other Engineering Managers and product development leadership to scope and prioritize platform work Set the quality bar for your team. Lead by example. Leadership Interview (1 hour) - With our head of engineering and executive leadership. description: Company Overview Deepgram is the leading platform underpinning the emerging trillion-dollar Voice AI economy, providing real-time APIs for speech-to-text (STT), text-to-speech (TTS), and building production-grade voice agents at scale. More than 200,000 developers and 1,300+ organizations build voice offerings that are ‘Powered by Deepgram’, including Twilio, Cloudflare, Sierra, Decagon, Vapi, Daily, Cresta, Granola, and Jack in the Box. Deepgram’s voice-native foundation models are accessed through cloud APIs or as self-hosted and on-premises software, with unmatched accuracy, low latency, and cost efficiency. Backed by a recent Series C led by leading global investors and strategic partners, Deepgram has processed over 50,000 years of audio and transcribed more than 1 trillion words. There is no organization in the world that understands voice better than Deepgram. Company Operating Rhythm At Deepgram, we expect an AI-first mindset—AI use and comfort aren’t optional, they’re core to how we operate, innovate, and measure performance. Every team member who works at Deepgram is expected to actively use and experiment with advanced AI tools, and even build your own into your everyday work. We measure how effectively AI is applied to deliver results, and consistent, creative use of the latest AI capabilities is key to success here. Candidates should be comfortable adopting new models and modes quickly, integrating AI into their workflows, and continuously pushing the boundaries of what these technologies can do. Additionally, we move at the pace of AI. Change is rapid, and you can expect your day-to-day work to evolve just as quickly. This may not be the right role if you’re not excited to experiment, adapt, think on your feet, and learn constantly, or if you’re seeking something highly prescriptive with a traditional 9-to-5. The Opportunity Voice is the most natural modality for human interaction with machines. However, current sequence modeling paradigms based on jointly scaling model and data cannot deliver voice AI capable of universal human interaction. The challenges are rooted in fundamental data problems posed by audio: real-world audio data is scarce and enormously diverse, spanning a vast space of voices, speaking styles, and acoustic conditions. Even if billions of hours of audio were accessible, its inherent high dimensionality creates computational and storage costs that make training and deployment prohibitively expensive at world scale. We believe that entirely new paradigms for audio AI are needed to overcome these challenges and make voice interaction accessible to everyone. The Role As a Member of the Research Staff, you will pioneer the development of Latent Space Models (LSMs), a new approach that aims to solve the fundamental data, scale, and cost challenges associated with building robust, contextualized voice AI. Your research will focus on solving one or more of the following problems: Build next-generation neural audio codecs that achieve extreme, low bit-rate compression and high fidelity reconstruction across a world-scale corpus of general audio. Pioneer steerable generative models that can synthesize the full diversity of human speech from the codec latent representation, from casual conversation to highly emotional expression to complex multi-speaker scenarios with environmental noise and overlapping speech. Develop embedding systems that cleanly factorize the codec latent space into interpretable dimensions of speaker, content, style, environment, and channel effects -- enabling precise control over each aspect and the ability to massively amplify an existing seed dataset through “latent recombination”. Leverage latent recombination to generate synthetic audio data at previously impossible scales, unlocking joint model and data scaling paradigms for audio. Endeavor to train multimodal speech-to-speech systems that can 1) understand any human irrespective of their demographics, state, or environment and 2) produce empathic, human-like responses that achieve conversational or task-oriented objectives. Design model architectures, training schemes, and inference algorithms that are adapted for hardware at the bare metal enabling cost efficient training on billion-hour datasets and powering real-time inference for hundreds of millions of concurrent conversations. The Challenge We are seeking researchers who: See "unsolved" problems as opportunities to pioneer entirely new approaches Can identify the one critical experiment that will validate or kill an idea in days, not months Have the vision to scale successful proofs-of-concept 100x Are obsessed with using AI to automate and amplify your own impact If you find yourself energized rather than daunted by these expectations—if you're already thinking about five ideas to try while reading this—you might be the researcher we need. This role demands obsession with the problems, creativity in approach, and relentless drive toward elegant, scalable solutions. The technical challenges are immense, but the potential impact is transformative. It's Important to Us That You Have Strong mathematical foundation in statistical learning theory, particularly in areas relevant to self-supervised and multimodal learning Deep expertise in foundation model architectures, with an understanding of how to scale training across multiple modalities Proven ability to bridge theory and practice—someone who can both derive novel mathematical formulations and implement them efficiently Demonstrated ability to build data pipelines that can process and curate massive datasets while maintaining quality and diversity Track record of designing controlled experiments that isolate the impact of architectural innovations and validate theoretical insights Experience optimizing models for real-world deployment, including knowledge of hardware constraints and efficiency techniques History of open-source contributions or research publications that have advanced the state of the art in speech/language AI Ideal Researcher Profile An ideal researcher, as evidenced by the recurring themes across these foundational papers, excels in five key areas: (1) Statistical & Mathematical Foundations, (2) Algorithmic Innovation & Implementation, (3) Data-Driven & Scalable Systems, (4) Hardware & Systems Understanding, and (5) Rigorous Experimental Design. Below is a synthesis of how each paper highlights these qualities, with references illustrating why they matter for building robust, impactful deep learning models. 1. Statistical & Mathematical Foundations Mastery of Core Concepts Many papers, like Scaling Laws for Neural Language Models and Neural Discrete Representation Learning (VQ-VAE), reflect the importance of power-law analyses, derivation of novel losses, or adaptation of fundamental equations (e.g., in VQ-VAE's commitment loss or rectified flows in Scaling Rectified Flow Transformers). Such mathematical grounding clarifies why models converge or suffer collapse. Combining Existing Theories in Novel Ways Papers such as Moshi (combining text modeling, audio codecs, and hierarchical generative modeling) and Finite Scalar Quantization (FSQ's adaptation of classic scalar quantization to replace vector-quantized representations) show how reusing but reimagining known techniques can yield breakthroughs. Many references (e.g., the structured state-space duality in Transformers are SSMs) underscore how unifying previously separate research lines can reveal powerful algorithmic or theoretical insights. Logical Reasoning and Assumption Testing Across all papers—particularly in the problem statements of Whisper or Rectified Flow Transformers—the authors present assumptions (e.g., "scaling data leads to zero-shot robustness" or "straight-line noise injection improves sample efficiency") and systematically verify them with thorough empirical results. An ideal researcher similarly grounds new ideas in well-formed, testable hypotheses. 2. Algorithmic Innovation & Implementation Creative Solutions to Known Bottlenecks Each paper puts forth a unique algorithmic contribution—Rectified Flow Transformers redefines standard diffusion paths, FSQ proposes simpler scalar quantizations contrasted with VQ, phi-3 mini relies on curated data and blocksparse attention, and Mamba-2 merges SSM speed with attention concepts. Turning Theory into Practice Whether it's the direct preference optimization (DPO) for alignment in phi-3 or the residual vector quantization in SoundStream, these works show that bridging design insights with implementable prototypes is essential. Clear Impact Through Prototypes & Open-Source Many references (Whisper, neural discrete representation learning, Mamba-2) highlight releasing code or pretrained models, enabling the broader community to replicate and build upon new methods. This premise of collaboration fosters faster progress. 3. Data-Driven & Scalable Systems Emphasis on Large-Scale Data and Efficient Pipelines Papers such as Robust Speech Recognition via Large-Scale Weak Supervision (Whisper) and BASE TTS demonstrate that collecting and processing hundreds of thousands of hours of real-world audio can unlock new capabilities in zero-shot or low-resource domains. Meanwhile, phi-3 Technical Report shows that filtering and curating data at scale (e.g., "data optimal regime") can yield high performance even in smaller models. Strategic Use of Data for Staged Training A recurring strategy is to vary sources of data or the order of tasks. Whisper trains on multilingual tasks, BASE TTS uses subsets/stages for pretraining on speech tokens, and phi-3 deploys multiple training phases (web data, then synthetic data). This systematic approach to data underscores how an ideal researcher designs training curricula and data filtering protocols for maximum performance. 4. Hardware & Systems Understanding Efficient Implementations at Scale Many works illustrate how researchers tune architectures for modern accelerators: the In-Datacenter TPU paper exemplifies domain-specific hardware design for dense matrix multiplications, while phi-3 leverages blocksparse attention and custom Triton kernels to run advanced LLMs on resource-limited devices. Real-Time & On-Device Constraints SoundStream shows how to compress audio in real time on a smartphone CPU, demonstrating that knowledge of hardware constraints (latency, limited memory) drives design choices. Similarly, Moshi's low-latency streaming TTS and phi-3-mini's phone-based inference highlight that an ideal researcher must adapt algorithms to resource limits while maintaining robustness. Architectural & Optimization Details Papers like Mamba-2 in Transformers are SSMs and the In-Datacenter TPU work show how exploiting specialized matrix decomposition, custom memory hierarchies, or quantization approaches can lead to breakthroughs in speed or energy efficiency. 5. Rigorous Experimental Design Controlled Comparisons & Ablations Nearly all papers—Whisper, FSQ, Mamba-2, BASE TTS—use systematic ablations to isolate the impact of individual components (e.g., ablation on vector-quantization vs. scalar quantization in FSQ, or size of codebooks in VQ-VAEs). This approach reveals which design decisions truly matter. Multifold Evaluation Metrics From MUSHRA listening tests (SoundStream, BASE TTS) to FID in image synthesis (Scaling Rectified Flow Transformers, FSQ) to perplexity or zero-shot generalization in language (phi-3, Scaling Laws for Neural Language Models), the works demonstrate the value of comprehensive, carefully chosen metrics. Stress Tests & Edge Cases Whisper's out-of-distribution speech benchmarks, SoundStream's evaluation on speech + music, or Mamba-2's performance on multi-query associative recall demonstrate the importance of specialized challenge sets. Researchers who craft or adopt rigorous benchmarks and "red-team" their models (as in phi-3 safety alignment) are better prepared to address real-world complexities. Summary Overall, an ideal researcher in deep learning consistently demonstrates: A solid grounding in theoretical and statistical principles A talent for proposing and validating new algorithmic solutions The capacity to orchestrate data pipelines that scale and reflect real-world diversity Awareness of hardware constraints and system-level trade-offs for efficiency Thorough and transparent experimental practices These qualities surface across research on speech (Whisper, BASE TTS), language modeling (Scaling Laws, phi-3), specialized hardware (TPU, Transformers are SSMs), and new representation methods (VQ-VAE, FSQ, SoundStream). By balancing these attributes—rigorous math, innovative algorithms, large-scale data engineering, hardware-savvy optimizations, and reproducible experimentation—researchers can produce impactful, trustworthy advancements in foundational deep learning. description: Op duizenden werkvloeren in Nederland wordt dagelijks gewerkt met gevaarlijke stoffen. Dat kan veilig, als je weet wat je in huis hebt, wat het doet en welke regels erbij horen. description: Op duizenden werkvloeren in Nederland wordt dagelijks gewerkt met gevaarlijke stoffen. Dat kan veilig, als je weet wat je in huis hebt, wat het doet en welke regels erbij horen. Daar helpt Sdu Toxic organisaties bij. Toxic is de meest complete SaaS-oplossing voor wet- en regelgeving rond gevaarlijke stoffen in Nederland. Organisaties registreren er hun stoffen mee, beoordelen blootstelling, leggen maatregelen vast en informeren hun medewerkers. Zo helpen we QHSE-professionals om mensen veilig te laten werken en aan de arbowetgeving te voldoen. Achter Toxic staat een team met diepgaande kennis van chemische producten en de regels die erbij horen. En een succesvol marketing- en salesteam dat zorgt dat steeds meer organisaties ons vinden. Toxic is onderdeel van Lefebvre Sdu, dat al 200 jaar bouwt aan juridische en fiscale kennis, en van Lefebvre Group, de Europese leider op dat gebied. De vraag groeit. Onze Commercieel Medewerkers Binnendienst en marketing plannen meer afspraken in dan we nu kunnen afronden. Daarom zoeken we een Senior Accountmanager die van die gesprekken klanten maakt. HOE JIJ ONS VERDER BRENGT Jij bent het gezicht van Toxic. Voor de veiligheidskundigen, managers en directies die met ons werken, word jij degene die ze kennen en vertrouwen. Je leert hun organisatie kennen, luistert naar wat er speelt en denkt mee over wat ze nodig hebben. Zo bouw je relaties die jaren meegaan, en groeit Toxic met je klanten mee. Je leert je klanten kennen: hun mensen, hun processen en wat er bij hen speelt. Zo word je hun vaste gesprekspartner en denk je mee over de volgende stap. Elke nieuwe relatie begint met een goed gesprek. De binnendienst en marketing plannen de afspraken, jij bereidt je voor en ontdekt wat een organisatie nodig heeft. Daarnaast zoek je zelf nieuwe kansen. In je demo's laat je zien hoe Toxic werkt en wat het oplevert. Gaat de vraag verder dan het standaardplatform? Dan werk je met collega's een oplossing op maat uit, met API-koppelingen en AI-toepassingen. Je bouwt relaties met veiligheidskundigen, inkopers en directie, brengt hun belangen samen in 1 voorstel en sluit deals met een hogere dealwaarde. Met strategische accountplannen houd je overzicht op je belangrijkste klanten. Je ziet kansen voor up- en cross-sell en herkent retentierisico's vroeg. Samen met Customer Success zorg je dat nieuwe klanten goed starten. Je houdt je pipeline en forecast actueel in Salesforce en deelt wat je bij klanten hoort met marketing en product. Als senior ben je mentor en sparringpartner voor collega-accountmanagers. DIT ZOEKEN WIJ Je bent iemand bij wie klanten zich gehoord voelen. Hello there! We’re Appinio, a global market research company that combines an AI-powered insights platform with expert consultancy. On a mission to make the world a little more fact-based, we help companies understand how consumers think and make smarter decisions.

We started out in Hamburg back in 2014, but we’re now humbled to call the world our playground, with over 260 employees spread across 13 countries (we’re remote-first), 2600+ international clients, delivering research from +190 markets, globally.

Want to be a part of the Appinio movement? 🚀

Here at Appinio, we value transparency in our recruitment process, and we've created a blog to share what to expect during each step of our journey together: here

Your mission as a Senior Research Consultant

We are looking for a Senior Research Consultant (m/f/d) with a strong quantitative market research background to join our newly dedicated B2B research team in the DACH region.

This specialized unit focuses on research projects that specifically survey B2B target groups, professional decision-makers, and niche business audiences (rather than only standard B2C consumer panels).   • Vision Components: Develop and integrate learning-based vision components, such as object detection, segmentation, and pose estimation, that give robots the input they need to grasp and manipulate objects.
  • Software Architecture: Design and implement software components, architectures, and applications for AI-enhanced robotic systems.
  • Robot Integration: Bring applications onto a changing range of robots and sensors, including dual-arm and humanoid platforms.
  • Research Transfer: Follow current research in computer vision and robot learning, and evaluate which external models and components are ready to integrate into the stack.
  • Stack Maintenance: Review, test, and maintain the shared software stack so that existing applications keep running as new components are added.

Essential Skills

  • Background: Degree in robotics, computer vision, computer science, electrical or mechanical engineering, or a related field, or equivalent experience, with around four years of professional experience building robotics or vision software.
  • Computer Vision: Hands-on experience training, adapting, and deploying current learning-based vision models, including pretrained vision and vision-language models, on real camera data.
  • ROS 2: Professional experience developing robotics software with ROS 2.
  • Programming: Production experience in C++ and Python, working with CMake, Git, and shell scripting.

Beneficial Skills

  • Vision-Based Manipulation: Experience using camera input to guide grasping or manipulation, for example grasp pose estimation or visual servoing.
  • Humanoid Platforms: Experience developing software for dual-arm or humanoid robots.
  • Motion Control: Working knowledge of robot motion planning and control.
  • Task Logic: Experience structuring robot task logic with state machines or behavior trees.

What we offer

  • A dynamic high-tech company, combined with financial soundness and world-class investors.
  • Join an interdisciplinary, international team with 60+ different nationalities in a collaborative work environment.
  • Lots of development opportunities as we continue to grow.

Agile Robots is a leading provider of AI-powered robotics solutions. By combining artificial intelligence and robotics, the company makes industries smarter, more flexible, and more efficient. 

Founded in Munich in 2018 by renowned robotics researchers from the German Aerospace Center (DLR), Agile Robots has experienced rapid global growth. Today, more than 3,500 highly skilled robotics and AI enthusiasts are employed worldwide. The company has one of the largest research and development teams in the AI and robotics industry. 

Agile Robots has built a unique portfolio; together with the subsidiaries BÄR Automation, Franka Robotics, idealworks, and Krause Automation, the company covers all areas of AI-driven robotics.

You are likely to bring deep expertise in either commodities and energy trading or data, analytics and AI, together with some understanding or practical exposure to the other. You will work alongside specialists from both disciplines, building on your core expertise while continuing to deepen your capabilities across the intersection of trading and AI. The aim is to turn emerging AI capabilities into practical, measurable improvements in how trading businesses operate.

AI & Trading Transformation

  • Shape propositions at the intersection of commodity trading, AI and digital transformation, and bring market insight on how AI is changing trading organisations, business models and competitive dynamics
  • Translate real trading problems into practical GenAI and agentic use cases that deliver value to clients
  • Advise clients on where AI should augment human decision-making, where workflows can be automated, and where human judgement remains critical
  • Design trading journeys from opportunity identification and experimentation through to scaled adoption, with the metrics and value cases that show impact on performance, productivity, risk and profitability
  • Work with traders, portfolio managers, data scientists and technology teams to turn concepts into solutions that operate in live trading environments
  • Drive adoption of GenAI copilots, agents and intelligent workflows that improve trader productivity and decision quality
  • Establish governance, model risk, human oversight and responsible-use approaches without losing sight of commercial outcomes

Commodities & Energy Trading

  • Advise on front-to-back trading processes, from market intelligence and trade origination through execution, scheduling, settlement and risk management across commodities including Power, Oil & Refined Products, Natural Gas, LNG, Metals, Renewables and Environmental Products
  • Support clients in evolving their trading strategies, operating models and capabilities in response to changing markets and new technologies
  • Bring an understanding of market structure, pricing, forecasting, physical flows and the commercial decisions that drive trading performance

 
Your skills and experience 

We are looking for an experienced professional with 8-12+ years of relevant experience and a strong background in either commodities and energy trading or data, analytics and AI. The strongest candidates will combine meaningful experience across both areas. However, we also welcome applicants who bring deep expertise in one discipline alongside a working understanding of, or some practical exposure to, the other.

You might be a commodities and trading specialist who has applied data, analytics or AI to trading decisions, processes or transformation, or a data and AI practitioner who has worked in, or gained exposure to, commodities, energy or another trading environment.

You do not need equal depth in both disciplines, but you should be able to demonstrate a genuine foundation in each and a clear motivation to deepen your experience at their intersection.
